critical_bugs: Position averaging logic in update_label resets historical mean when new_observations=0 (default), because n = max(0, 1) = 1. This breaks persistent position tracking over time.
Pickle deserialization in _load() lacks validation or safe unpickling guards, creating an arbitrary code execution risk if the registry file is corrupted or tampered with.
warnings: Broad except Exception block in _load() swallows specific errors (e.g., EOFError, UnpicklingError), making it difficult to diagnose data corruption.
No file locking or concurrency controls; simultaneous access from multiple robot processes could cause race conditions during read/write cycles.
Running average calculation assumes total_observations accurately tracks position updates, which may drift if observation counts differ from actual position measurements.
recommendations: Replace pickle with JSON or a lightweight database (e.g., SQLite) to eliminate security risks, improve data integrity, and enable cross-language compatibility.
Fix update_label to only recalculate mean_position_m when new_observations > 0, or maintain a dedicated position_update_count field separate from general observations.
Validate root_path using os.path.abspath() and restrict traversal outside the intended workspace directory to prevent unintended path access.
Implement explicit schema version checking during _load() with migration logic to gracefully handle future format changes.
